blocks.explanation:
Yeh bilkul kitab ke Example 29 jaisa sawal hai: algebraic \(x\) aur trigonometric \(\cos 2x\) ka product.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
ILATE mein A pehle aur T baad mein, is liye \(x\) first function hai; differentiate ho kar woh sirf 1 ban jata hai.
\(\cos 2x\) second function hai, jis ka integral \(\frac{\sin 2x}{2}\) hai.
Plan: ek dafa parts, phir \(\int \sin 2x\,dx\) jo seedha aata hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int x\cos 2x\,dx\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: integration by parts: \(f(x) = x\) aur \(g(x) = \cos 2x\).

Parts lagayein
\[= x\cdot\dfrac{\sin 2x}{2} - \int \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\cdot 1\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\int \sin 2x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\cos 2x\) ka integral \(\frac{\sin 2x}{2}\) hai, kyunke \(\sin 2x\) ko differentiate karein to chain rule se 2 ka factor aata hai, us ko khatam karne ke liye 2 se divide kiya. \(x\) ka derivative 1.

\(\sin 2x\) ka integral
\[= \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{\cos 2x}{2}\right) + c\]
\[= \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4} + c\]
Kyun: \(\int \sin 2x\,dx = -\frac{\cos 2x}{2}\). Bahar ka minus aur andar ka minus mil kar plus ban gaye.
Dhyan dein: \(\sin\) ka integral \(-\cos\) hota hai; yeh minus bhoolne se jawab mein \(-\frac{\cos 2x}{4}\) aa jata hai, jo ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2} + x\cos 2x - \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\]
\[= x\cos 2x\]
Kyun: product rule aur chain rule lagaye; \(\frac{\sin 2x}{2}\) wale terms cancel ho gaye aur integrand wapas aa gaya.
